title: Karma School Loop: Notebook Edition
premise: A humorous time-loop school day game where the player relives one day in eight actions, steering karma, relationships, crime consequences, and small social dramas.
interaction_model: Single-screen mobile-friendly branching choice game with tap-based scene decisions, notebook tabs for people/activities/map, and modal social/activity interactions.
objective: Guide the repeated school day toward better karma and stronger relationships while avoiding arrest, handling injuries, and experimenting with the loop's social and chaotic options.
progression: Each day contains 8 timed action slots; choices alter karma, relationship percentages, injury state, location context, and crime heat, then the loop resets into a new day with discovered characters and relationships retained.
theme: School life, teen comedy, karma, romance, delinquency, and time-loop experimentation.
mood: Playful, scribbly, mischievous, light, and occasionally chaotic.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy casual narrative games, humorous school-life sims, choice-based loops, and low-pressure social stat management on mobile or web.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a choice-based school day time-loop with karma and relationship management.
High confidence that replayability comes from repeating 8-step days, unlocking people, and exploring good-versus-chaotic runs.
Moderate confidence that there is no final hard win state implemented; the experience appears to emphasize expressive runs rather than definitive completion.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first browser game called "Karma School Loop: Notebook Edition," presented as a single-screen, choice-driven school-day time loop with a hand-drawn notebook aesthetic. The player relives one day over and over, and each day contains exactly 8 actions mapped to times like Wake Up, Commute, Homeroom, Classes, Lunch, Afternoon, Clubs, and Evening. Every scene should show a big emoji, a bold title, a short humorous description, and 2 to 4 large tap-friendly choices. Choices should adjust a karma meter ranging from bad to good, affect relationship percentages with discovered characters, sometimes raise crime heat, and occasionally cause injury. Include a notebook side menu with three tabs: People, Acts, and Map. People should list discovered characters with bond meters and allow modal interactions like Chat, Compliment, Prank, Fight, and unlocking Ask Out once a bond threshold is reached. Acts should offer side activities such as crime, social posting, and self-care, each with randomized outcomes. Map should let the player visit locations like School, Home, Store, and Doctor, with location-specific scenes that persist until the player leaves. If the player commits too many crimes or triggers an instant-arrest outcome, shift the rest of the day into a jail mini-loop with different scenes. If the player gets badly hurt in a fight, show an injury status that blocks some physical actions until the Doctor cures it. At the end of the 8th action, play a sleep/reset transition, increment the day counter, clear temporary location and wanted state, soften karma slightly toward neutral, and begin the next loop. Use playful teen-comedy writing, emoji-forward presentation, reaction toasts, light sound feedback, and a cozy-but-chaotic mood that mixes wholesome social choices, romance attempts, school absurdity, and delinquent consequences.
